content.user_title: Design Apple HIG Menus and Buttons
content.value_statement: Menu and button choices can become inconsistent across Apple platforms. This skill applies Apple HIG guidance to choose, place, label, and organize menus, buttons, and toolbars.
actual_capabilities: Recommends menu, button, toolbar, and disclosure components based on Apple HIG guidance.
Explains when to use context menus, edit menus, dock menus, pull-down buttons, and pop-up buttons.
Provides platform-specific guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS where available.
Suggests menu organization, item ordering, labeling, shortcuts, destructive actions, and toolbar placement.
Cross-references related HIG topics for search, controls, dialogs, inputs, and platform interaction patterns.
limitations: It does not replace review against the latest Apple documentation or platform SDK behavior.
It does not generate production UI code by itself.
It focuses on Apple platform components, not web or Android design systems.
It cannot validate screenshots or prototypes unless the user provides them.

use_cases.title: Choose the Right Component
use_cases.description: Compare menus, buttons, and toolbars before adding a command to an Apple app interface.

use_cases.title: Review Platform Behavior
use_cases.description: Check menu bar, toolbar, and button expectations before implementing iOS, iPadOS, or macOS screens.

use_cases.title: Audit Interface Consistency
use_cases.description: Review existing commands, labels, destructive actions, and shortcuts against Apple HIG recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for choosing one UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am designing an Apple app screen with these actions: [actions]. Which menu or button component should I use, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Toolbar
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of toolbar structure and priority.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this toolbar plan for [platform]: [toolbar items]. Recommend ordering, grouping, overflow behavior, and any missing menu support.

prompt_templates.title: Design Menus Across Platforms
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for multiple Apple platforms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create menu and command guidance for [app type] across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Include context menus, menu bar items, shortcuts, and destructive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Command System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit of an existing interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this command model against Apple HIG menus and buttons: [commands, screens, platforms]. Identify mismatches, risks, and concrete design changes.

output_examples.input: Should delete, archive, and share actions be in one pull-down button?
output_examples.output: Use visible buttons for primary actions and reserve a pull-down button for secondary actions. Mark destructive items clearly and ask for confirmation.

output_examples.input: Where should a Mac document app place export and print commands?
output_examples.output: Place standard document commands in expected menu bar locations. Use toolbar buttons only for frequent actions, and keep menu access available.

output_examples.input: How should a visionOS toolbar handle many editing tools?
output_examples.output: Prioritize essential tools, avoid vertical toolbars, and keep controls accessible as windows resize. Move less common actions to suitable menus.

best_practices: State the target Apple platforms before asking for component guidance.
Provide the action list, priority, destructive behavior, and current screen context.
Ask for platform differences when designing shared iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, or visionOS flows.
anti_patterns: Do not hide primary actions inside context menus or pull-down buttons.
Do not use custom buttons when standard Apple components communicate the action clearly.
Do not make menu bar, toolbar, or shortcut access the only path to critical commands.

faq.question: Does this skill cover both menus and buttons?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers standard buttons, action buttons, pull-down buttons, pop-up buttons, menus, context menus, edit menus, dock menus, and toolbars.

faq.question: Can it help with macOS menu bars?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for menu bar structure, standard menus, dynamic menu items, Help menus, Window menus, and menu bar extras.

faq.question: Does it support visionOS guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Several references include visionOS behavior for buttons, context menus, toolbars, and menu placement.

faq.question: Will it generate SwiftUI or AppKit code?
faq.answer: Not directly. It provides design recommendations that can guide later implementation in SwiftUI, UIKit, or AppKit.

faq.question: How should I get the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the platform, screen purpose, action list, action priority, and whether any action is destructive.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
